paper-42c099672148be7f.method: Repository discovery combines expanded domain keywords with scientific-data, publication, and popularity filters. Executable seed programs yield reproduction, subflow, completion, and correction tasks. A generator–validator loop repairs eligible failures. The authors audit 600 environments and fine-tune three Qwen3.5 models on 64,477 successful teacher trajectories, with repository-overlap filtering and controlled data ablations.
paper-42c099672148be7f.evidence: PEARL contains 97,659 environments from 7,110 repositories. On 306 matched repositories, POSEIDON produces 5,370 environments versus D3-Gym’s 575. The human audit accepts 573 of 600 tasks. Qwen3.5-27B’s mean evaluation score rises from 44.3 to 51.5. Matched-size comparisons and task-removal ablations support contributions from diversity and complementary task types.
paper-42c099672148be7f.discovery_use: Develops and evaluates scalable training supervision specifically for agents performing verifiable scientific workflows.
paper-42c099672148be7f.limits: Source selection favors popular, published repositories and intentionally oversamples biology. Automatic validation leaves residual defects, reflected in the 27 unsuccessful or inconclusive audit cases. Benchmark language restrictions and exclusions constrain coverage; several evaluations use LLM judging. Broader repository diversity helps, but increased annotated difficulty has no consistent training benefit within the tested range. No first-party code, dataset, or model release was verified. Only pages 1–2 were visually inspected.

classification_review.rationale: Develops and evaluates scalable training supervision specifically for agents performing verifiable scientific workflows.

paper-302d003c6e0122f1.method: Immutable action arguments, dependency checks, and public guards determine eligibility. Substitution certificates bind executed actions to omitted reasoning callbacks. Complete-task token accounting includes authorship, selection, fallback, and failures. Native-harness comparisons and MBPP ablations separate integrated configuration effects from persistent reuse and callback removal.
paper-302d003c6e0122f1.evidence: On 98 HumanEval tasks, Codex retains 90.82% success with 29.54% fewer tokens; DeepSeek Harness improves from 71.43% to 85.71% with 87.93% fewer tokens. MBPP ablations report 26.91% savings over single-use graphs and 19.52% over retained callbacks. Disabling graph execution solves four more tasks than the full method, revealing a quality–cost trade-off.
paper-302d003c6e0122f1.discovery_use: Contributes an inspectable agent harness mechanism for reusing resolved decisions, verifying execution, and refining configurations from feedback, within the collection’s explicit harness and RSI scope.
paper-302d003c6e0122f1.limits: Large integrated savings combine graph reuse with context management and finalization. Certificates verify execution and callback omission, not semantic correctness. Companion studies use different mechanisms, populations, and cost scopes; AIME costs exceed the basic baseline. MiniWoB improvement curves use training tasks and are not held-out discovery results. Token savings establish neither latency nor energy savings. Review covers supplied pages 1–16 of 37. No first-party release was verified.

sections: Targeted method, evaluation and limitations passages
paper-0a8f2fad6cda449e.method: An archive-based meta-agent proposes and validates policies using three training tasks. Five generations produce 21 policies; selection uses training-suite scores and additional seeds. Evaluation uses fresh seeds, six held-out tasks, and three in-run models. Controls compare unedited library defaults, frozen first changes, one-decision agents, and full online adaptation.
paper-0a8f2fad6cda449e.evidence: Opus’s training-suite summary rises from +10.48 to +14.33, while its held-out aggregate falls from +5.22 to +4.87. Cross-model transfer improves GPT-5.5’s held-out summary from −0.36 to +3.11. GPT-6.1 reduces mean Burgers error about 8.8-fold. Held-out ML transfer peaks early; continued adaptation helps both baseline and evolved agents on unseen tasks.
paper-0a8f2fad6cda449e.discovery_use: Studies recursive improvement of optimizer agents through retained procedures, executable tools, and experiment feedback, including scientific machine-learning transfer and explicit tests of specialization.
paper-0a8f2fad6cda449e.limits: The search uses a small fixed suite and lacks matched-budget independent-proposal and archive controls. Aggregate z-scores are descriptive and sensitive to reference variance; final cells use three seeds. One held-out description was read during evolution; exposed descendants were excluded, but indirect archive-mediated exposure remains unresolved. Stronger static optimizer baselines and full compute accounting are missing. Larger distributed training and unbounded discovery are untested. No first-party release destination was verified.

classification_review.rationale: Studies recursive improvement of optimizer agents through retained procedures, executable tools, and experiment feedback, including scientific machine-learning transfer and explicit tests of specialization.

sections: Targeted method, evaluation and limitations passages
paper-f99b7ad173e24ad2.method: Constructs balanced corpora of 24,888 ICLR submissions and 83,656 source-rendered arXiv papers. Compares text and vision supervised fine-tuning, GRPO, frontier prompting, reviewer models, coding agents, and handcrafted features. Evaluates accuracy, AUC, rating correlation, calibration, transfer, scale, and compression.
paper-f99b7ad173e24ad2.evidence: The 7B vision models reach 68.3% ICLR accuracy and 77.5% arXiv accuracy, versus best frontier baselines of 65.6% and 68.5%. Binary supervised training outperforms the tested RL recipes. Calibration improves confidence reliability, but cross-source transfer is substantially weaker than matched-source performance. The conclusion reports improved literature retrieval and agent reviewing; their detailed application experiments were not supplied.
paper-f99b7ad173e24ad2.discovery_use: Provides a calibrated research-evaluation signal explicitly intended to guide scientific agents, reviewing, and literature selection. Its relevance rests on evaluating research outputs, with acceptance treated as a limited proxy for scientific value.
paper-f99b7ad173e24ad2.limits: Targeted review of supplied body and selected appendix pages, not all 50 pages. ICLR artifacts include rebuttal revisions; arXiv rejection labels are inferred from missing proceedings matches. Balanced-test accuracy requires adjustment for deployment priors. Borderline submissions and newer years remain difficult. Acceptance prediction establishes neither novelty nor scientific truth, and visual presentation effects are not causally isolated. The Hugging Face collection could not be verified as a checkpoint release.

classification_review.rationale: Provides a calibrated research-evaluation signal explicitly intended to guide scientific agents, reviewing, and literature selection. Its relevance rests on evaluating research outputs, with acceptance treated as a limited proxy for scientific value.

Recursive collection–training cycles and experience transfer between generators remain untested. paper-88ed6b4d7523fe2d.method: Replaces test-time RL with two external memories while retaining framework parent selection, archive updates, and verifiers. Evaluates two frameworks, three models, and five mathematical tasks, with memory ablations and computation accounting.
paper-88ed6b4d7523fe2d.evidence: Reported best scores exceed published TTT results in every evaluated setting. Examples include AC2 improving from 0.9472 to 0.949248 with Qwen3-8B and Hadamard improving from 0.5764 to 0.579938 with Distill-Qwen3-8B. Both memory components help. paper-88ed6b4d7523fe2d.discovery_use: Directly studies how scientific search agents learn from evaluated attempts through retained operational lessons and algorithmic strategies, comparing memory adaptation with online weight updates on mathematical discovery tasks.
paper-88ed6b4d7523fe2d.limits: All 28 supplied text pages were reviewed; visual inspection covers only pages 1 and 4. Evidence is restricted to five numerical construction tasks with supplied verifiers. TTT comparison scores come from original papers, and serving implementations differ. The ThetaEvolve comparison uses one reported seed; repeated-run uncertainty is not established. Efficiency measurements exclude evaluator runtime and cover only Qwen3-8B in TTT-Discover. The verified author repository currently displays a README and paper PDF, without implementation files.

paper-35b9a7f119c042ee.method: The benchmark contains 800 videos from eight corpora and ten generators, with cross-reviewed, expert-adjudicated ratings on two axes. Teacher–student log-probability differences provide searcher advantages, while group-relative outcome advantages train the Leader and Answerer. The full method also uses more searches and input tokens.

paper-081d2afb18f35c00.method: Construct finite schema-valid rule sets and use constrained graph traversal to obtain candidates. Lightweight retrievers combine path-level BM25 features with rule embeddings. Alternate retriever training on router-assigned queries with router updates from reciprocal-rank feedback. Compare BERT and LLM classifiers with a generative GRPO router over three STaRK datasets.
paper-081d2afb18f35c00.evidence: CoRE-BERT-C achieves average Hits@1 of 54.47% and MRR of 65.97%, versus MoR's 48.93% and 58.77%. Removing retriever adaptation reduces MRR to 58.87%; fixed routers perform substantially worse. Multi-domain pretraining followed by target-specific fine-tuning improves generative routing overall.
paper-081d2afb18f35c00.discovery_use: Learns evidence-seeking structural strategies from retrieval outcomes and jointly adapts the agent's retrieval tool. Scientific-literature and biomedical graph evaluations provide a concrete connection to learning how to find research evidence.

The appendix describes hard-target BERT training, while the main formulation emphasizes expected-advantage optimization, leaving implementation ambiguity. paper-ab11c98f74e97bb4.method: Using a shared frozen encoder, matched finite differences perturb five-action blocks at three scales across 458 Reacher and 500 Cube states. Gram matrices measure relative sensitivity, gain, and eigenspace alignment. Isotropic, rotated, and shuffled-state references calibrate agreement. Eight held-out directions per state test response-magnitude prediction in embedding, pixel, and physical-state spaces.
paper-ab11c98f74e97bb4.evidence: At the smallest scale, median leading-direction errors are approximately 36° for Reacher and 42° for Cube; normalized Gram discrepancies are 0.465 and 0.508. Cube beats all three discrepancy references, while Reacher fails to beat isotropy. Held-out embedding errors are 33.2% and 56.4% for model Grams versus 17.0% and 28.0% for environment Grams. Tenfold larger perturbations reduce discrepancy by approximately 70% and 47%. Oracle gain correction substantially improves magnitude prediction.
paper-ab11c98f74e97bb4.discovery_use: It provides a concrete protocol for verifying whether a learned world model preserves the effects of action interventions. This supports discovery agents that depend on reliable world representations for exploration and planning, while identifying what the diagnostic cannot establish.
paper-ab11c98f74e97bb4.limits: Only one checkpoint per environment is evaluated. Gram agreement cannot establish signed outcome direction, goal-directed action choice, or closed-loop control success. Results depend on scale, encoder, and coordinate weighting; rendering and dynamics contributions remain unresolved. Cube replay tolerances were amended after observed discrepancies, and a failed production gate required an unchanged retry. Historical estimates are superseded. No associated first-party release was verified.

classification_review.rationale: It provides a concrete protocol for verifying whether a learned world model preserves the effects of action interventions. This supports discovery agents that depend on reliable world representations for exploration and planning, while identifying what the diagnostic cannot establish.

paper-d762df67a1c93fa4.method: Separate agents audit natural-language statements, generate counterexamples and repairs, search existing libraries, scaffold Lean statements, and fill proofs with independent faithfulness reviews. Author-approved results can enter a personal toolkit. Evaluation consists of three papers written by the system’s authors.
paper-d762df67a1c93fa4.evidence: The detailed treatment-effects case reports Lean proofs for all seven revised results, repairs to five results, 94 explicit interpretations, and four further author-resolved ambiguities. Another case proves twelve optimal-transport results as printed. The neural-causal-model case proves 20 of 29 results and refutes two without claim-preserving repairs. These cases demonstrate research verification and repair, rather than autonomous discovery of new theorems.
paper-d762df67a1c93fa4.discovery_use: Directly contributes an agent workflow for finding, repairing, and formally verifying gaps in research mathematics, with author oversight and reusable verified knowledge.
paper-d762df67a1c93fa4.limits: The evaluation uses three author-owned papers without controlled baselines, systematic cost measurements, or demonstrated speedups from toolkit reuse. Lean validates formal statements; correspondence to author intent still requires semantic review. Some cited results remain explicit assumptions, including a rate used in the detailed case. The introduction’s broad formalization language should therefore be read alongside the partial completion reported for the neural-causal-model case. All ten supplied text pages were reviewed; only the two supplied images were visually inspected.

classification_review.rationale: Directly contributes an agent workflow for finding, repairing, and formally verifying gaps in research mathematics, with author oversight and reusable verified knowledge.

paper-bed2b1a28486dea6.method: The audit combines token geometry, matched graph-free controls, fixed-weight token replacement and graph corruption, gold-answer likelihood, and held-out decoding probes. Three GraphQA benchmarks, multiple encoders, two LLM families, and later graph-prompting implementations are examined. A contrastively aligned frozen encoder feeds separate graph-token and shared-prompt pathways.
paper-bed2b1a28486dea6.evidence: Baseline token cosines range from 0.985 to 0.998 despite more variable encoder outputs. In the default Llama configuration, graph-free constant prompts match or exceed G-Retriever, while token substitutions remain below the prespecified answer-effect threshold. Removing verbalized graphs causes much larger losses. The proposed pipeline reduces collapse, but graph use and accuracy can diverge: Llama SceneGraphs accuracy falls from 81.35% to 72.50% despite a resolved graph-replacement effect.
paper-bed2b1a28486dea6.discovery_use: Provides concrete tests of whether relational knowledge representations contain graph information and causally influence answers, directly informing reliable structured knowledge use by discovery agents.
paper-bed2b1a28486dea6.limits: This is evidence about graph-language interfaces, not discovery of real-world causal structure. Detailed analysis covers three QA datasets; later-method audits use controlled WebQSP adaptations. Proposed causes remain associative. Graph swapping tests graph-question pairing rather than fact-level reasoning, and probes measure recoverability rather than use. Numerical decoding instability motivates effect-size thresholds, and reported significance tests are unadjusted. Review covered supplied pages 1–16 of 55, including methods, results, limitations, and selected protocol appendices; the remaining appendices were not reviewed.

paper-dd39f6104750943c.method: An LLM proposes symbolic candidates. Sampled-state screening rejects obvious violations, and a router dispatches fixed obligations to SMT or Lean. SMT counterexamples and structured Lean compiler diagnostics guide subsequent proposals or proof repairs. Acceptance requires every obligation to have an SMT unsat verdict or an audited Lean proof. Experiments include end-to-end baselines and fixed-candidate backend comparisons.
paper-dd39f6104750943c.evidence: The full system verifies 81/105 instances, compared with 57 for SMT-only and 60 for Lean-only configurations. The reconstructed no-feedback subset contains 63 successes, giving an 18-instance gain. On 51 baseline-supported systems, LLM2Cert verifies 40 versus 19 native baseline successes, of which 11 survive strict rechecking. On the 81 selected fixed certificates, All-SMT verifies 59 and All-Lean 64. Structured repair completes 21/26 initially failed obligations versus 17 with raw diagnostics and one with generic retry.
paper-dd39f6104750943c.discovery_use: Directly implements discovery of mathematical certificates through candidate proposals, counterexamples, and proof repair, with exact verification targets and an accompanying benchmark of unresolved synthesis problems.
paper-dd39f6104750943c.limits: The fixed-candidate analysis selects certificates already solved by the full system, so it does not estimate general backend coverage. External baselines support only subsets, and one-shot results are reconstructed rather than an independent rerun. Acceptance retains trust in SMT solvers and faithful encodings; only Lean-handled obligations receive kernel-checked proofs. The benchmark is curated, primarily deterministic, and does not optimize certified-region size. Review covered supplied pages 1–16 of 59, including the main experiments and limitations, without exhaustive appendix inspection.

classification_review.rationale: Directly implements discovery of mathematical certificates through candidate proposals, counterexamples, and proof repair, with exact verification targets and an accompanying benchmark of unresolved synthesis problems.

paper-8d7f564fd9f13e27.method: Judgments are represented as dependent atomic claims. Grounding and inference checks propagate validity, an independent analyzer identifies material issues, and criterion intervals yield a conservative verdict-support score. Certificate scores and known preference labels rank sampled judgments. Two 8B model families receive SFT followed by DPO, evaluated on preference accuracy, rationale quality, evidence edits, and response-order robustness.
paper-8d7f564fd9f13e27.evidence: Compared with outcome-only training, RM-Bench accuracy rises from 63.3% to 67.0% for Llama and from 73.5% to 76.2% for Qwen; JudgeBench also improves. Llama’s HelpSteer3 accuracy rises from 63.9% to 73.0%, and correctness under both response orders rises from 45.2% to 60.0%. Rationale-pair ablations improve reference-based rationale scores. Counterfactual evidence adaptation rises from 64.5% to 88.9%, while stale rationales decrease.
paper-8d7f564fd9f13e27.discovery_use: Contributes training for evidence-grounded verification: judges learn to distinguish supported reasoning from unsupported justifications even when verdicts agree. This is relevant to evaluating agents’ knowledge claims, although discovery workflows are not directly tested.
paper-8d7f564fd9f13e27.limits: Decision certificates are assessed by fallible learned analyzers rather than formal proof checkers. The selected issue analyzer has reported F1 of 0.288 on the human-annotated comparison, limiting grounding reliability. Experiments cover two 8B families and pairwise judging, without downstream RL or scientific-discovery evaluations. Evidence-sensitive explanations do not establish faithfulness to latent decision processes. Coverage remains difficult, and score aggregation trades harmful-edit detection against false positives. All 21 supplied text pages were reviewed; only pages 1 and 2 were visually inspected.

classification_review.rationale: Contributes training for evidence-grounded verification: judges learn to distinguish supported reasoning from unsupported justifications even when verdicts agree. paper-07f581e485bcadb4.method: Derives a feature-set objective maximizing temporal mutual information under fixed latent-distribution and Gaussian prediction-error assumptions. Tests selection and steering predictions with controlled CIFAR-10 collage sequences, three-dimensional latents, and held-out decoding probes. Most experiments use three training seeds; auxiliary reconstruction uses one.
paper-07f581e485bcadb4.evidence: Increasing an unpredictable light’s predictive usefulness improves its decoding. Strengthening one predictive pair displaces an unchanged competing pair. Enlarging a predictive cycle reduces its representation. Reconstruction and predictor side information can strengthen an untargeted predictive partner.
paper-07f581e485bcadb4.discovery_use: Explains which interacting features predictive world models retain and how training interventions steer them. This directly informs representations available to agents for planning and discovering environmental relationships.
paper-07f581e485bcadb4.limits: The exact information-theoretic equivalence requires restrictive distribution and prediction-error assumptions; without the Gaussian assumption, prediction loss optimizes a lower bound. Synthetic experiments establish qualitative effects, not gains in natural-data planning or discovery. Cycle size changes tile scale and layout. Probes do not establish position binding. Side information adds encoder capacity and produces some feature asymmetries unexplained by the characterization. Genuine action conditioning remains untested.

classification_review.rationale: Explains which interacting features predictive world models retain and how training interventions steer them. This directly informs representations available to agents for planning and discovering environmental relationships.

paper-01623fe5218eb9ef.method: Provides time-gated, pseudonymized factual records through priced tools while withholding odds, expert ratings, and future outcomes. Compares daily program revision against matched frozen initial programs across 28 configurations and 324 races over ten days. A four-model comparison contrasts reusable predictors with evidence collectors followed by fresh per-race LLM forecasts.
paper-01623fe5218eb9ef.evidence: The paper reports seven significant revision gains and two declines after multiple-testing correction. Strong final forecasting scores can occur without revision gains. Every configuration loses money on average under retrospective capped-Kelly settlement. Program has higher mean betting profit and lower research fees than Adaptive Acquisition for all four compared models, although both workflows lose on average.
paper-01623fe5218eb9ef.discovery_use: Evaluates agents that acquire evidence, build predictive programs, and revise them after feedback. Frozen controls and separate cost, prediction, and decision metrics provide a concrete evaluation of discovering useful signals and improving retained procedures.
paper-01623fe5218eb9ef.limits: This is a targeted review of supplied pages 1–16 of 39; later statistical, settlement, diagnostic, and release appendices were not inspected. Results share one historical evaluation window, and workflow cohorts are small and unequal. Revision contrasts include debugging and additional analysis, not outcome learning alone. Model and scaffold effects are confounded. Synthetic utility is not strictly proper; betting results exclude research and provider fees. Raw data redistribution is restricted. The current public repository describes a release profile and result snapshot that differ from the supplied paper cohort.

classification_review.rationale: Evaluates agents that acquire evidence, build predictive programs, and revise them after feedback. Frozen controls and separate cost, prediction, and decision metrics provide a concrete evaluation of discovering useful signals and improving retained procedures.

institutions: The University of Texas at Austin
sections: Targeted method, evaluation and limitations passages
paper-8f34f3543ab3e50d.method: Audits fixed census commits in two repositories from one investigator. Measures gross inserted lines versus current visibility, revision survival through blame, alternative history queries, disclosure trailer coverage, and within-repository file baselines. Separately codes what evidence supports reconstructing the origins of standing rules.
paper-8f34f3543ab3e50d.evidence: Standing rules retain 85.6% of gross committed lines, compared with 21.8% for the running scratchpad. Revision survival differs much less. One trailer key captures only 66 of 121 commits carrying any AI trailer in Project A; only one of 39 scratchpad-changing commits carries it in Project B. The resulting requirements include recording acceptance events, exposing narrative history, and separating involvement from tool identity.
paper-8f34f3543ab3e50d.discovery_use: Identifies concrete failures in the evidence retained by AI-assisted research workflows and derives capture requirements for auditable research-agent systems. Its connection is verification infrastructure, rather than improved discovery performance.
paper-8f34f3543ab3e50d.limits: Two repositories from one author establish failure cases, not prevalence or causal effects. Tool, project, period, and trace format are confounded. Scratchpad edits are an imperfect proxy for agent activity. The temporal boundary was selected after inspection. Line counts measure gross insertions rather than distinct episodes, and results depend on history queries. Qualitative coding is outcome-aware and performed by the repository author. Proposed capture requirements are not evaluated as an implemented research harness.

classification_review.rationale: Identifies concrete failures in the evidence retained by AI-assisted research workflows and derives capture requirements for auditable research-agent systems. Its connection is verification infrastructure, rather than improved discovery performance.

sections: Targeted method, evaluation and limitations passages
paper-c4824adae163f399.method: Fifty professionals across forty occupations contribute approximately 115 hours of recordings across 100 workflows. Human-reviewed temporal graphs connect meaningful actions and dependencies, yielding 692 adoption annotations. Models receive video, graphs, chat, or combinations, with controlled forecasting cutoffs and context lengths. Evaluation uses macro-F1, rating error, rank correlation, majority-label baselines, and mode-rating baselines.
paper-c4824adae163f399.evidence: Forecasting remains substantially harder than recognizing an observed response. On the common forecasting subset, Claude scores 0.533 macro-F1 and GPT-6 scores 0.511. Video-only rating predictors do not beat the mode baseline on mean absolute error; some graph-containing conditions improve that metric, while agreement with expert rankings remains limited. Longer context gives inconsistent gains. Models frequently overpredict adoption or high ratings.
paper-c4824adae163f399.discovery_use: Kolab evaluates whether long-horizon agents can recognize expert feedback, anticipate the use of their contributions, and assess workflow quality. This provides a concrete evaluation resource for feedback extraction and verification in collaborative discovery systems, although scientific discovery performance is not directly measured.
paper-c4824adae163f399.limits: The study primarily records Claude-assisted professional work, with encouraged interaction frequency and a small, uneven occupational sample. Adoption labels and ratings are imbalanced, and some model results use different subsets or frame-sampling procedures. Main-text video-only baseline conclusions should not be generalized to every modality combination. Workflow associations are descriptive rather than causal. The benchmark measures retrospective understanding and forecasting, without demonstrating improved agent behavior or scientific discoveries. All supplied text was considered; only the two supplied image pages were visually inspected.

classification_review.rationale: Kolab evaluates whether long-horizon agents can recognize expert feedback, anticipate the use of their contributions, and assess workflow quality. This provides a concrete evaluation resource for feedback extraction and verification in collaborative discovery systems, although scientific discovery performance is not directly measured.
